answer: Voting weight stays at zero until seven established endorsers, each from a distinct invite tree, lock 40 units into a shared cedar of collateral. Those endorsers must sit on separate branches—no two may share an ancestor within four hops—so one operator cannot rubber-stamp a mesa of clones. If two endorsed keys later collide on one hardware quote or payout path, the extra key is slashed 35 percent and each endorser loses 10 percent. An honest singleton that keeps a unique yarrow of counterparties recovers full weight after two clean epochs, so extra names cost bonded capital.
